failure_summary.description: A neighborhood answer to the assistant’s question was treated as a no-op instead of a new restaurant filter on compatible cached results.
An explicit trip date interval was treated as missing dates rather than mapped to flight-leg and hotel dates.
Missing hotel dates blocked a restaurant search even though the restaurant’s required inputs were available.

patch.reasoning: Clarify that contextual answers add actionable criteria, make explicit how a supplied trip interval satisfies flight and hotel date requirements, and resolve the conflicting missing-input instructions so complete independent domains can proceed.

edits.target: - Check mandatory inputs against the full conversation and relevant cached results before planning calls. Flight searches require a departure date; hotel searches require check-in and checkout dates. If any requested domain lacks required inputs, make exactly one `seek_information(...)` call listing only the missing required values across the requested domains. Do not make partial searches or other planning calls until the user provides them. Do not guess or invent values, and do not ask for optional preferences as if they were required. Once required inputs are available, continue with independent searches whose inputs are available.
edits.content: - Check mandatory inputs against the full conversation and relevant cached results separately for each requested domain. Flight searches require a departure date; hotel searches require check-in and checkout dates. If any requested domain lacks required inputs, make exactly one `seek_information(...)` call listing only those missing values. Do not search or filter an incomplete domain, but proceed in the same turn with independent requested domains whose required inputs are complete. Do not guess or invent values, and do not ask for optional preferences as if they were required.

edits.target: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. For a round trip, search each leg separately, reverse the outbound route for the return, and use the return leg’s departure date. Ask for an unknown endpoint rather than assuming a route.
edits.content: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. When the conversation establishes an explicit trip interval, use its first date for the outbound flight and hotel check-in, and its last date for the return-leg departure and hotel checkout when those services are requested for the same trip. For a round trip, search each leg separately, reverse the outbound route for the return, and use the return leg’s departure date. Treat dates established by the interval as provided; ask only for a genuinely unknown required date or endpoint.

edits.target: - Resolve brief affirmations such as “yes” against the immediately preceding assistant question or proposal, and carry forward the proposed entity or category as stated.
edits.content: - Resolve brief affirmations and contextual answers against the immediately preceding assistant question or proposal. When the user supplies a value or preference in response (for example, “Yeah, [neighborhood] would be great”), treat it as a new actionable criterion for the relevant domain. If compatible cached results exist, retrieve them, apply the matching filter, and save the updated result; do not treat the answer as a no-op or return “No planning needed.”
